newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUNESS SAYS ENGLISH GAME TAKING ITS TOLL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUNESS SAYS ENGLISH GAME TAKING ITS TOLL.

text.p: Southampton manger Graeme Souness said on Wednesday the punishing nature of English soccer was taking its toll on his foreign stars.
Last month's arrival of Israeli schemer Eyal Berkovic, Norwegian striker Egil Ostenstad and Dutch defender Ulrich Van Gobbel sparked the premier league club into an eight match unbeaten run.
Berkovic was outstanding when Southampton fans enjoyed their most exhilarating afternoon in years late last month as champions Manchester United were thrashed 6-3.

With the powerful Ostenstad grabbing a hat-trick against Alex Ferguson's men, and Van Gobbel a tower of strength at the back, Souness looked to have proved there was more to his side than Matt Le Tissier.
But in the 7-1 defeat at Everton, Saturday's 2-0 home reverse against Leeds, and Tuesday's fortunate 1-1 League Cup draw at first division Oxford, all three failed to make any significant impact.
Berkovic's subdued display led to him being hauled off before the end, and Souness said he believed the sheer pace of the English game was now being felt by all three.
"I actually think the game is quick on the continent, at certain times, but the difference is that it's quick here for 90 minutes.
"It's there all the time, like having somebody attacking you round the throat who you can't pull away. There's no chance of a rest."

But Souness added: "That's English football, what makes it so attractive. There are no dull moments. In foreign football there are lulls in the game, but here there's something happening all the time."
